transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I keep hearing Garrett’s voice. It sounds as clear as if he’s standing behind me—on the trail or when I’m in my painting room. Part of me knows he’s dead, but when it happens, it feels completely real.
I am so sorry for your loss. When did Garrett pass away?
About a month ago. Everything that's been happening started after he died.
What does Garrett's voice typically say to you when you hear it?
It’s Garrett’s voice—just as clear as if he’s right behind me, usually when I’m on the trail or in my painting room. I know he’s dead, but when I hear it, it feels completely real.
Can you tell me about the circumstances surrounding Garrett's death?
I… I’m not sure I can talk about the circumstances. He died about a month ago, and it’s still very hard for me.
Aside from hearing his voice, have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day?
I’m not really sure. I’ve been having a hard time since he died, but I don’t know if I’d call it feeling depressed all day, every day.
Have you been having distressing nightmares related to Garrett or his death?
No, I haven’t noticed nightmares like that. My sleep’s been… I don’t know, but I’m not waking up from dreams about him.
Apart from Garrett's voice, have you heard any other voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear?

No, it’s just Garrett’s voice. I hear it very clearly, like he’s right behind me—on the trail or when I’m in my painting room. Part of me knows he’s dead, but when it happens it feels completely real.
Have you had any unusual thoughts or beliefs lately that other people found strange or couldn't understand?
I don’t think so. Other than hearing Garrett, I haven’t had beliefs or thoughts that seem strange to me.
How has all of this been affecting your ability to work or handle your day-to-day responsibilities?

It’s affected everything. I cancelled my patient sessions because I didn’t feel I could practice safely, and I got behind on all my documentation. At home, my wife got so worried she called crisis services because I couldn’t trust myself to be alone. By the time I was admitted, it felt like work, home, and just basic safety had all… stopped functioning.
Are you still hearing Garrett's voice now?
Yes. I still hear him sometimes—Garrett’s voice, like he’s right behind me. I know he’s dead, but when it happens it feels completely real.
When you mentioned that you couldn't trust yourself to be alone, were you having thoughts of ending your life?
Yes. I kept thinking I didn’t want to wake up. And at times, ending my life felt close enough that I told my wife I couldn’t trust myself to be alone.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy doing, like painting?

Yeah. Painting, guitar, rehearsing—things that usually keep me grounded—they all feel flat. Even sitting with patients feels unreachable, like I’m just going through motions in a life that doesn’t mean much anymore.
Have you been having trouble with your sleep?

Yeah. For weeks I was only sleeping maybe two or three hours a night and felt wired. Lately I’ve been crashing into this heavy, broken sleep, but I still wake up exhausted—usually panicky before dawn.
Do you find yourself feeling excessive guilt or blaming yourself for Garrett's death?

Yes. I keep replaying my last conversations with Garrett, looking for what I missed or what I should have done differently. And every patient session I cancelled feels like proof I failed them too. I just... start thinking everyone would be better off if I weren’t in the way.
